title: Making Decisions with Inversions
author: The Effective Project Manager
summary: This short 'Effective Project Manager' newsletter introduces Charlie Munger's inversion technique as a faster, less exhausting way for project managers and other decision-makers to improve their choices: instead of asking how to succeed, ask how you would fail, then avoid those specific pitfalls. The author illustrates the method with Warren Buffett's practice of identifying 'the dumbest mistakes' he could make in investing and applies it to team collaboration, reframing 'how do I improve collaboration' as 'how do I destroy teamwork' to surface concrete risks like poor communication and ignored feedback.
points: Introduces Charlie Munger's 'invert, always invert' technique for faster, lower-effort decision-making.
Applies inversion specifically to team collaboration by asking 'how do I destroy teamwork' to surface concrete failure modes.
Cites Warren Buffett's practice of naming 'the dumbest mistakes' he could make as a real-world use of the same method.
Frames inversion as broadly transferable across project management, business, and personal decisions.
quotes: Instead of asking, "How do I succeed?", ask, "How do I fail?" Then, simply avoid those pitfalls.
Instead of "How do I improve my team's collaboration?", ask "How do I destroy teamwork?" The answers, poor communication, lack of transparency, ignoring feedback, show exactly what to avoid.
Warren Buffett applies it to investing, asking, "What are the dumbest mistakes I could make?" and then ensuring he avoids them.
Next time you face a tough choice, invert the problem. Identify what would make things worse, then steer clear.
Inversion flips problem-solving on its head, revealing risks and blind spots you might otherwise miss.
